title: GDScript: An introduction to dynamic languages
key_points: GDScript is a dynamically typed language with advantages such as ease of use, quick code changes, readability, no compilation required for testing, and runtime efficiency.
In GDScript, variables are 'variant'-like meaning their type can change through assignment.
Function arguments in GDScript can be of different types.
GDScript uses pointers and references similarly to C++ and Java, allowing functions to modify objects passed as parameters.
limitations: Less performance than statically typed languages due to dynamic typing.
More difficult to refactor code because symbols can't always be traced.
Errors that would normally be detected at compile time only appear at runtime in GDScript.
asserts: GDScript is designed to allow games to be created quickly and efficiently, with the option to use C++ for computationally intensive parts.
